summary.title: Obtaining historical and real-time crypto data with very simple web programming
summary.one_liner: You learn how to pull real-time and historical BTC-USD (and other pair) exchange rates from the CryptoCompare API using small HTML and JavaScript web apps.
keywords: build crypto trading bot with r
pagination of api results backward in time
takeaways: A simple CryptoCompare price endpoint returns the current exchange rate for a pair such as BTC to USD.
A JavaScript fetch loop can refresh a price every 10 seconds in a plain HTML page.
Historical endpoints (histohour, histoday) return up to 2000 points per call, so you page backward with toTs to cover longer periods.
The free API key is limited in the number of calls, and log-scale plots reveal the dampening of Bitcoin's peak gains over time.
summary.summary: The author, a scientist, explains how to fetch cryptocurrency exchange rates from the CryptoCompare API with minimal programming. The article presents two browser-based apps: one that refreshes the BTC-USD price every 10 seconds, and one that retrieves minute, hour, or day historical data by repeatedly calling the API backward in time (up to 2000 entries per call, with a free API key). It then shows example plots of Bitcoin's daily price history, including a log10 plot, and offers interpretive commentary that the author labels as subjective. The page includes disclaimers that it is not financial advice and links to further reading. The page also notes an alternative keyless API added later.
